A condition where credit forces a borrower into a cycle of debt where repayment requires selling assets.

A corporation that owns or controls production facilities in more than one country.

definitions.definition: A comprehensive process involving economic growth, higher per capita income, equitable distribution, and improvements in non-material life parameters like health, education, freedom, and security.
Development that satisfies current human needs without compromising the capacity and natural assets of future generations.
The total market value of all final goods and services produced within a country during a specific financial year.
definitions.source_reference: Chapter 2: Sectors of the Indian Economy

definitions.definition: A labor market state where more people are employed in a work activity than necessary, so the marginal contribution of extra workers is zero.
definitions.source_reference: Chapter 2: Sectors of the Indian Economy

definitions.definition: Any item or verifiable record generally accepted as a medium of exchange for goods and services and repayment of debts.
The complete set of conditions agreed upon between lender and borrower, including interest rate, collateral, documentation, and repayment schedule.
The process of rapid economic integration and interconnection among countries driven by international trade, cross-border investment, and technological connectivity.
definitions.source_reference: Chapter 4: Globalisation and the Indian Economy

definitions.definition: A traditional market doctrine meaning 'let the buyer beware', placing sole responsibility on consumers prior to consumer protection laws.

concepts.explanation: Developmental goals differ among individuals; progress for one group can cause destruction or loss of livelihood for another.
Per capita income hides wealth distribution disparities and excludes essential health, education, and environmental parameters.
Only final goods value is included in GDP calculations because intermediate goods costs are already incorporated in the final sale price.
concepts.source_reference: Chapter 2: Sectors of the Indian Economy

concepts.explanation: The Tertiary sector grew to contribute over 50% of Indian GDP, but labor migration out of Agriculture lagged, leaving >44% labor in Primary sector.
concepts.source_reference: Chapter 2: Sectors of the Indian Economy

concepts.explanation: Commercial banks retain ~15% of deposits as cash reserves and lend out ~85%, earning profit from the spread between loan and deposit interest rates.
Credit generates surplus and income growth when productive (virtuous), but leads to debt traps and asset loss when crop/business failure occurs (vicious).
MNCs break production into specialized processes across countries to optimize labor costs, raw material access, and technical skill.
concepts.source_reference: Chapter 4: Globalisation and the Indian Economy

concepts.explanation: Globalisation benefits affluent urban consumers and skilled IT professionals while forcing small producers into bankruptcy and casualizing labor.
concepts.source_reference: Chapter 4: Globalisation and the Indian Economy

concepts.explanation: COPRA provides a structured legal court system (District, State, National) based on monetary claim thresholds to resolve consumer complaints.

facts.fact: World Bank classifies high-income countries as those with Per Capita Income exceeding USD 49,300 per annum (2021 data).
India's Per Capita Income was USD 2,370 per annum in 2021, placing it in the low-middle income category.
Kerala has an Infant Mortality Rate of 7 per 1,000 live births compared to Haryana's 30 and Bihar's 32.
Kerala has a Literacy Rate of 94% compared to Haryana's 80% and Bihar's 62%.
Primary sector in India employs over 44% of the workforce but contributes less than 16% to Gross Value Added (GVA).
facts.source_reference: Chapter 2: Sectors of the Indian Economy

facts.fact: MGNREGA 2005 guarantees 100 days of wage employment per year to rural households willing to do unskilled manual work.
facts.source_reference: Chapter 2: Sectors of the Indian Economy

facts.fact: Commercial banks in India hold about 15% of their total cash deposits as liquid reserves for daily withdrawals.
December 24 is observed as National Consumers Day in India to mark the presidential assent to COPRA in 1986.
Under COPRA 2019 rules, District Commissions handle claims up to ₹1 Crore, State Commissions ₹1 Crore to ₹10 Crore, and National Commission > ₹10 Crore.

people.role_significance: Father of the Nation; quoted regarding sustainable resource stewardship: 'The Earth has enough resources to meet the needs of all but not enough to satisfy the greed of even one person.'
Founder of Grameen Bank of Bangladesh; awarded the 2006 Nobel Peace Prize for pioneering micro-credit for poor rural women without formal collateral.
Small farmer owning a 2-hectare unirrigated plot, representing the typical case study of rural disguised unemployment.
people.source_reference: Chapter 2: Sectors of the Indian Economy

people.role_significance: Shoe manufacturer in festive order case study illustrating a positive/virtuous credit outcome.
Small groundnut farmer illustrating crop failure, high interest moneylender credit, and the vicious debt trap.
Bank housing loan borrower illustrating formal credit terms including interest rate, salary documentation, and collateral.
Class IX student from Kerala paralyzed due to medical anesthesia negligence; case study demonstrating the Right to Safety under COPRA.
Consumer who bought a defective wall clock without obtaining a cash bill; case study highlighting the necessity of receipts for legal claims.
Small capacitor manufacturer in Hosur whose business failed due to cheap duty-free foreign imports after 1992 liberalisation.

India adopts landmark Economic Liberalisation reforms, removing foreign trade barriers.

Nobel Peace Prize awarded to Prof. Muhammad Yunus and Grameen Bank of Bangladesh.
Major amendment and updating of Consumer Protection Act (COPRA 2019) in India.

institutions.role_function: National standards body issuing ISI Mark for industrial goods and Hallmark for precious metals.

Apex quasi-judicial consumer court in New Delhi handling claims exceeding ₹10 Crore and appeals from State commissions.

cause_effect.cause: Excessive tube-well groundwater extraction exceeding natural rainfall recharge.

cause_effect.cause: Removal of import duties on capacitors in 1992 after liberalisation.
cause_effect.effect: Inability of small Indian producers (like Ravi in Hosur) to compete with cheap MNC imports, leading to plant closures.

cause_effect.cause: Surplus family labor engaged on small, unirrigated agricultural plots.
